content.title: Identity Board Variant | Fixed Reference, Multi-Angle Stage Proof
content.summary: This is an evidence variant of the existing recurring identity board. Keep one original reference board or strip fixed in one screen region while an original clearly adult character performs in a separate active stage. Use at least four genuinely different identity proofs—full-body walk, side or overhead geometry, face close-up, hand-object relation or one customized action—while the board remains unchanged. Major transitions may use one lens occlusion but must return to the same anchors. End with board and complete character visible together. Do not copy source character, sheet, outfit, yellow set, typography, choreography or timing.

quick_start.input_format: Keep one original reference board fixed in the same screen region throughout. + Separate the fixed board from an active performance stage. + Use at least four different proof classes including full body, hard angle, face and gesture or object relation. + After any occlusion or camera stress, return to the same board anchors and adult identity. + End with complete adult character and board visible together.
quick_start.recommended_input: Keep one original aerospace-mechanic reference strip fixed along the left edge: adult face front and profile, cobalt coverall seams, copper wrist band and white helmet stripe. On the active stage, the same adult enters a neutral gray hangar. Move to a controlled overhead harness rotation while the strip never changes; preserve helmet stripe, shoulder width and tool-hand relation through the difficult angle. After occlusion, reveal the complete same adult beside one original short mark BAY FOUR while the unchanged reference strip remains visible; no source character, yellow stage, costume, letters or logo.

usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.

slots.name: lead_subject
slots.constraint: An original stable subject or pair with a readable role.

slots.name: setting
slots.constraint: A new setting with fixed spatial anchors and no source-specific surface.

slots.name: escalation_variable
slots.constraint: One causal variable that changes through visible stages.

slots.name: performance_rule
slots.constraint: A restrained acting or motion rule that keeps the mechanism legible.

slots.name: camera_grammar
slots.constraint: An information order that proves each state without copying source shot boundaries.

slots.name: payoff
slots.constraint: A clean final physical, informational or social consequence.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.constraint: An original hierarchy of diegetic cues; no unsupported source-audio claim.

anti_copy_exclusions: source character sheet, adult model, face, red outfit and body proportions
source yellow stage, floor and backdrop
source walk, pose, top-down descent and lens-reaching choreography
source large letters, creator logo and terminal mark
source MiniMax H3 thread prompt, camera path, timing and creator identity
